title: Look at the light
line: Seven mornings, one minute of light before the phone.
intro: In Athena’s reading of Plato’s Sun simile, the eye is the most sun-like organ and stores the sun’s light, and the soul carries a small sun within. Athena counts waking up and looking at the sun among the ways to make yourself lovable, since eros is woken by beauty. For seven mornings, give the first minute of your day to the light: the light, never the sun itself.
does: Each morning, before the phone, look at the morning light for one minute.
trains: Beginning the day turned towards the light rather than the screen.
each: Before you touch the phone, open the curtains or step outside and look at the morning light for one minute: the sky, the light on walls, roofs and leaves. Look at the light, never straight into the sun. If you wake in the dark, do it when the first light comes.
note: What was the light like this morning, and what did it wake in you?
end: After seven mornings: what has the first minute of light changed in how your days begin?
